dct_description_sm: Recently, an increase in spring and summer air temperature, precipitation, and ice-free period as well as a decrease in winter snow depth, and sea-ice extent and thickness has been reported for Hudson Bay and other areas in the Canadian Arctic. The evolutionary adaptations of ringed seals, and other ice-breeding seals (bearded and harbour seals) to exploit the land-fast ice habitat for reproduction and survival could expose this species to critical challenges with predicted global warming and changes in sea ice extent. Recent studies have illustrated the negative role of early ice break-up and decreasing snow depth on the condition and survival of ringed seals.  Given the evidence of ecosystem structure changes linked to reductions in the duration of the ice cover period, we aimed to:  1) Describe and summarize movement and diving behaviour of ringed seals and assess their relationships with sea ice concentration, bathymetry, and marine productivity indices.                                                                                                                                                2) Delineate areas of intense ringed seal foraging behaviour and investigate the role of demography and changes in oceanographic environment in this process.
dct_title_s: Ringed seal satellite telemetry in Hudson Bay and Foxe Basin
